note: Recast from the original description of Froggatt 1898 (in English), published there as Termes krisiformis n.sp.; the alate is not described in the original, which covers the soldier and the worker, and the type locality is Torrens Creek, northern Queensland, Australia (collected by J. H. Chisholm, 7 specimens). The original gives body length in lines (1 line = 1/12 inch ≈ 2.12 mm), the converted value being added in parentheses. The worker description is cut off in the scanned text and the last sentence is transcribed only as far as the break.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head very elongate and slenderly cylindrical, the posterior part slightly rounded, the sides straight and rising abruptly as far as the mandibular base at the antennal base; the frons projecting, wrinkled and overhanging the clypeus; the mandibles are not directed straight forward but are raised first and then bent down, of uneven thickness, the tip bent into a hollow drill-like point; the pronotum very narrow with a truncate anterior margin.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale yellow; mandibles rust-coloured; pronotum pale yellow, the rest dirty white. Body length 3 lines (about 6.35 mm). Head very elongate and slenderly cylindrical, the posterior part slightly rounded; the sides straight, rising abruptly as far as the mandibular base at the antennal base; a suture crosses the head and joins a transverse suture, forming a horn-shaped mark in the middle; the frons projecting, wrinkled, overhanging the clypeus. Antenna 14 segments, arising from a cleft in line with the front of the head and the mandibular base; segment 1 very large, rounded at the end; segments 2 and 3 about equal in length; segment 4 the smallest, oval; segments 5—13 oval, becoming pear-shaped and larger towards the tip; segment 11 the longest, oval. Labrum long, wide at the base, slightly narrowed towards the tip, truncate at the tip, with a point on each side. Mandibles narrow and very slender at the base, raised upward instead of directed straight forward, then bent down again, of uneven thickness, the tip bent into a hollow drill-like form and contracted into a point. Pronotum very narrow, the anterior margin truncate, the sides rather angular and curving round towards the tip; legs fairly long, the femora stout, the tibiae short, with two stout apical spines, the claws large. Abdomen elongate oval, the cerci slender.
